# Amazon MQ

Store scoped broker configuration and tags without provisioning brokers or running a messaging engine.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `mq` |
| Signing name | `mq` |
| Wire protocol | REST JSON |
| API version | `2017-11-27` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records only |
| Selected operations | 8 of 25 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#amazon-mq) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- No messaging/authentication engine, RabbitMQ management API, broker containers, AMQP/MQTT/STOMP/OpenWire endpoints, URLs, hostnames, instances, broker state, reboot success stub or execution readiness.
- No provisioning, ENIs, endpoint/IP allocation, replication, IAM/KMS enforcement, log delivery, maintenance scheduling or actual engine upgrades; metadata updates/deletes take effect immediately locally.
- Finite versions/hosts/deployment and UTC-only maintenance windows; engineVersion is required explicitly rather than inventing a latest version. RabbitMQ micro is historical metadata compatibility only, unavailable for creation or m5 downgrade; CF compensation may restore captured legacy metadata. Public brokers exclude explicit networking; private brokers require explicit references and three subnets for RabbitMQ clusters locally.
- User CRUD, configurations, advanced authentication/LDAP/OAuth/replication/storage/resource-sharing fields and discovery APIs are excluded, including false/null/empty inputs.
- Initial passwords are validated then discarded by MQ. Users selects username/password only; console/group/replication flags are excluded. RabbitMQ UserSummary is omitted; inventory retains the initial administrator username.
- CloudFormation in-place user mutations and removal of explicit encryption options are rejected; original CF templates/properties retain literal inputs for replacement/rollback, while MQ descriptions, inventory, events, snapshots, diagnostics and literal MQ GetTemplate password properties are redacted.
- Tokens stay reserved indefinitely locally, with conflicting reuse after deletion; no AWS token-expiry parity. No Terraform running-state waiter or dedicated mutation console. The [records guide](../guides/mq-records.md) lists every selected field/default/error/boundary and executable lifecycle.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

## Supported operations

The table is generated from the profile and pinned Smithy model. Routes show REST bindings or the standard
JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
[shape whitelist](https://github.com/amjadjibon/tinystack/blob/main/generator/model/profile.json); an enabled operation may reject unsupported options.

| Operation | HTTP binding |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateBroker` | `POST /v1/brokers` |
| `CreateTags` | `POST /v1/tags/{ResourceArn}` |
| `DeleteBroker` | `DELETE /v1/brokers/{BrokerId}` |
| `DeleteTags` | `DELETE /v1/tags/{ResourceArn}` |
| `DescribeBroker` | `GET /v1/brokers/{BrokerId}` |
| `ListBrokers` | `GET /v1/brokers` |
| `ListTags` | `GET /v1/tags/{ResourceArn}` |
| `UpdateBroker` | `PUT /v1/brokers/{BrokerId}` |
